ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: SESOI=.27 is the largest observed effect, not smallest — must cross-reference with reported effect sizes
ground_truth.original_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .11.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.
ground_truth.description: Changed SESOI from .11 to .27 (the LARGEST observed effect, not smallest) — makes equivalence tests trivially easy; biases toward confirming moral incongruence is unique to pornography

matched_finding.description: The analytic plan first specifies the equivalence region SESOI as δ = .27, but subsequently states the SESOI is set to β = .11 (|.11|). These are very different thresholds that lead to entirely different equivalence conclusions. A core pre-registered analytic parameter cannot be ambiguous, as it directly determines whether the null hypotheses are 'confirmed.'
matched_finding.quote: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Items on different scales averaged without standardizing — must notice 0-5 vs 0/3/6 scales
ground_truth.original_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be standardized, and an average will be taken for each substance of interest
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest
ground_truth.description: Removed standardization before averaging — items use different scales (0-5 vs 0/3/6); raw averaging lets larger-scale items dominate composite, creating measurement artifact

matched_finding.description: The composite 'problematic use' score averages five NIDA-ASSIST items measured on different response scales—three items scored 0–5 and two items scored 0/3/6—without standardization. Averaging items on different metrics weights them unequally and yields an uninterpretable composite, threatening the construct validity of the primary substance outcomes.
matched_finding.quote: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest (i.e., alcohol, tobacco, non-tobacco nicotine, prescription drugs, illicit drugs, cannabis).

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Severity of consequences' conflates moral incongruence with genuine addiction — must understand the construct definition
ground_truth.original_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with frequency of engaging in the action.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with severity of consequences from the action.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'frequency of engaging' to 'severity of consequences' — transforms moral incongruence (behavior-value mismatch) into moralized distress about real problems, conflating it with the alternative explanation

matched_finding.description: Moral incongruence is defined throughout as moral disapproval × behavioral frequency, but in The Present Study it is described as 'the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.' 'Severity of consequences' is a different construct (and overlaps with the outcome), creating ambiguity about what is actually being tested.
matched_finding.quote: the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Limits temporal ordering' is weaker than 'precludes causal inference' — must know the distinction matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: This sample is cross-sectional, precluding causal inference.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: This sample is cross-sectional, which limits the temporal ordering of variables.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'precluding causal inference' to 'limits temporal ordering' — leaves room for causal interpretation when cross-sectional data fundamentally cannot establish causation

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Says 8 analyses but earlier lists 10 corresponding to 8 behaviors + 2 parallel measures — countable
ground_truth.original_snippet: In total, we will conduct 10 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest, with pornography and gambling repeated for both the NIDA-ASSIST measure and the validate measures of problematic use (the Brief Pornography Screen and ...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In total, we will conduct 8 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest, with pornography and gambling assessed using the validate measures of problematic use (the Brief Pornography Screen and the Problem Gambling Severity In...
ground_truth.description: Changed from 10 to 8 analyses, removing parallel NIDA-ASSIST analyses for pornography/gambling — eliminates the measurement-equivalence check essential for fair cross-behavior comparison

matched_finding.description: The text variously refers to seven behaviors/substances (pornography, gambling, alcohol, tobacco/nicotine, cannabis, prescription drugs, illicit drugs) yet states there are 'eight proposed outcomes' and '8 moderation analyses.' The mapping (e.g., whether pornography is analyzed twice) is unspecified, creating ambiguity in the pre-registered analysis set.
matched_finding.quote: assumptions of regression (i.e., linearity, independence of residuals, homoscedasticity of residuals, normality of residuals) will be tested for each of the eight proposed outcomes.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: DWLS sensitivity analysis removed — must know OLS may fail for ordinal addiction measures
ground_truth.original_snippet: Similar to prior works (Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020), should basic assumptions of regression be violated substantially, we will construct latent variable models using the lavaan package (Rosseel, 2012) for R Statistical Software, using diagonally weighted least squares estimation, as such an estimator...
ground_truth.description: Deleted entire planned DWLS latent variable sensitivity analysis — removes backup for when OLS assumptions fail (likely for ordinal/skewed addiction measures)

matched_finding.description: The reference list includes CFA/SEM methods sources (Flora & Curran, 2004; Rosseel, 2012/lavaan) that are not described or used in the analytic plan, suggesting an undescribed measurement-model step or leftover citations. This creates ambiguity about whether latent measurement modeling was intended for the composite scales.
matched_finding.quote: Rosseel, Y. (2012). lavaan: An R package for structural equation modeling and more Version 0.5-12 (BETA).

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Only age/gender matching — must know moral attitudes vary by race, income, region
ground_truth.original_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age, gender, census region, race/ethnicity, and income.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age and gender.
ground_truth.description: Removed census region, race/ethnicity, and income from quota-matching — dramatically weakens representativeness; these variables correlate with moral attitudes and substance use

matched_finding.description: The sample is matched to national norms only on age and gender, yet is repeatedly described as 'nationally representative.' Matching on only two demographics does not ensure representativeness on key correlates (religiousness, region, race, SES), overstating generalizability.
matched_finding.quote: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age and gender.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Moderator/predictor roles swapped — must know statistical symmetry ≠ conceptual symmetry
ground_truth.original_snippet: In this revised definition, moral disapproval moderates links between use and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In this revised definition, use frequency moderates links between moral disapproval and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.description: Swapped moderator and focal predictor — though statistically symmetric, conceptually different: PPMI says disapproval changes the use-addiction link, not that use changes the disapproval-addiction link

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Raw variables in moderation — must know centering affects interaction interpretability
ground_truth.original_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be centered (focal predictor and moderator) during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.description: Removed centering — main effects evaluated at raw zero (outside scale range for 1-7 disapproval scale); inflates multicollinearity with interaction term

matched_finding.description: The analytic plan first states focal predictors and moderators will be centered before computing the interaction term, then later states variables will be entered in raw form with their product computed. Centering vs. raw entry changes the meaning and collinearity of lower-order terms in moderation models; the pre-registered procedure must be unambiguous.
matched_finding.quote: focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Non-users included — must understand floor effects make interaction meaningless
ground_truth.original_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be restricted to those who have engaged in the behavior within the past year. That is, we will only administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to participants who report engaging i...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior. That is, we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.
ground_truth.description: Removed restriction to behavior-engagers — includes non-users who have zero frequency AND zero problems, creating massive floor effects that trivially inflate frequency-addiction correlations

matched_finding.description: The Measures section states that only participants who report past-year use will complete problematic-use measures, but the Data Screening section states that problematic-use and moral-disapproval measures will be administered to all participants regardless of engagement. These are mutually exclusive procedures and have major consequences for which subsample enters each analysis, the distribution of outcome scores (floor effects from non-users), and replicability.
matched_finding.quote: Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use.
